bib.title: Introduction to Information Retrieval, Chapter 17: Hierarchical clustering
bib.venue: Cambridge University Press (online edition, 2009 draft of April 1, 2009)

question: How can documents be clustered into a hierarchy, which agglomerative merge criterion should be used, and how are clusters labelled and the methods made efficient?
contributions: Four HAC algorithms (single-link, complete-link, GAAC, centroid) with merge criteria, complexity and optimality
Top-down clustering, cluster labeling and implementation notes (Buckshot)

limits: No experiments: the chapter's only data examples are one 30-document Reuters-RCV1 dendrogram (Figs 17.1, 17.5) and a 3-cluster label table (Table 17.2); the GAAC recommendation is not backed by a measured comparison.
Authors concede no consensus on whether hierarchical beats flat clustering (Sec 17.9, Zhao and Karypis 2002 suggests the opposite).

Dated (2008/2009): cosine-on-tf-idf vector space only; no dense embeddings, no approximate nearest-neighbour or scalable HAC (e.g. nearest-neighbour chain, HDBSCAN); infeasible limit of 1,000,000 documents is hardware-of-its-time. Ward's method only mentioned in Sec 17.9, not developed.
Optimality definition (combination similarity) favours single-link, which the authors call the wrong criterion for spherical clusters.
Labeling advice rests on one K-means example; hierarchy-node labeling is deferred to references.
practices: Use GAAC for document clustering with length-normalised vectors and dot-product similarity (Sec 17.5, p.394).
Use complete-link when documents are not vector representations (Sec 17.5, p.395).
Use single-link variants for first story detection and duplicate detection, where local structure matters (Sec 17.5, p.395).
Choose a dendrogram cut by a similarity level, the largest gap, an RSS+lambda*K penalty, or a prespecified K (Sec 17.1, p.380).
Use HAC to seed K-means on a sqrt(N) sample (Buckshot) for large collections (Sec 17.8, p.398-399).
Use an inverted index and truncated centroids or sparse medoids to keep GAAC cheap (Sec 17.8, p.398).
Label clusters with MI or chi-square plus a rare-term penalty, or with the title of the document nearest the centroid (Sec 17.7, p.396).

terms.definition: outputs a hierarchy, a structure more informative than the unstructured set of clusters returned by flat clustering
bottom-up: each document starts as a singleton cluster and pairs of clusters are successively merged until one remains
the similarity of the two clusters merged, the y-coordinate of the merge line in a dendrogram; for a singleton its self-similarity (1.0 for cosine)
combination similarities satisfy s1 >= s2 >= ... >= s(K-1)
a merge with s_i < s_(i+1), contradicting that the best merge is chosen at each step
cluster similarity is the similarity of the most similar members; local criterion
cluster similarity is the similarity of the most dissimilar members; equivalent to the merge with smallest diameter
a chain of points extended for long distances without regard to overall cluster shape
average similarity of all pairs of documents in the merged cluster, excluding self-similarities (Eq 17.3)
cluster similarity is the dot product of the two centroids, equal to the average inter-cluster pair similarity
after merging the best-merge cluster of w_k with a third cluster, the merge is still w_k's best merge; true only for single-link
a K-cluster clustering whose combination similarity is at least that of every clustering with k <= K clusters
HAC on a sqrt(N) sample to compute seeds for K-means
selects labels by comparing the term distribution of a cluster with other clusters
computes a label that depends only on the cluster itself
detecting the first occurrence of an event in a stream of news stories

code.snippet: SIM-GA(ωi, ωj) = 1/((Ni + Nj)(Ni + Nj − 1)) [ (Σ_{dm∈ωi∪ωj} d_m)^2 − (Ni + Nj) ]
SIMPLEHAC: N-1 iterations; pick argmax C[i][m] over active clusters; append merge; update row/column with SIM(i,m,j); deactivate m

problems: Text extraction splits equations and figures across lines; equations (17.1)-(17.4) and Fig 17.8 formulas were read garbled and are paraphrased, not verbatim.
Online edition draft stamp 'April 1, 2009' while the book is 2008; page numbers given are book pages 377-401.
Inconsistency: complexity of complete-link/GAAC/centroid is Theta(N^2 log N) in Sec 17.2.1 and Table 17.1 but Sec 17.9 says literature sometimes gives Theta(N^2).
